newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescued yachtsman's family to welcome his return.
newsitem.headline: Rescued yachtsman's family to welcome his return.

text.p: The family of British yachtsman Tony Bullimore, dubbed the "miracle man" after his astounding rescue from freezing seas, plans to welcome him back to dry land early on Monday.
The Australian navy frigate Adelaide, which rescued Bullimore and fellow round-the-world solo sailor Thierry Dubois on Thursday, is on its way to Fremantle near Perth.
Bullimore's wife and other relatives have flown from Britain to meet him, while his 81-year-old aunt living in Perth has said she too plans to be there.
The yachtsmen and the sailors who rescued them have been hailed around the world as heroes and will be swamped by the media on arrival.
Bullimore's survival story is expected to attract huge commercial interest from newspapers, television and movie studios.
Australian media have quoted promotions experts as estimating Bullimore could expect to make A$2 million (US$1.6 million) from his rescue, the closest ever to Antarctica.
Agent Max Markson said on Sunday he was negotiating advertising endorsements for Bullimore and that movie offers had already been made.
A separate production house was interested in making a documentary and an Australian television network had already signed an exclusive deal to cover the reunion of Bullimore and his wife, he said.
Bullimore, 56, was rescued after surviving for four days in a dark air pocket in his upturned yacht, battered by Antarctic seas 2,600 km (1,600 miles) from Australia.
Dubois, a competitor in the same the Vendee Globe Challenge as Bullimore, was plucked by helicopter from a tiny life-raft dropped earlier by the Australian air force.
But after his return, Bullimore is likely to need surgery to repair his frostbitten fingers and toes and damage to a finger partly amputated during the ordeal.
